@graph.name: Casa Nina Flamingo
@graph.description: Casa Nina Flamingo is a newly built three-storey villa above Playa Flamingo on Costa Rica’s Guanacaste coast, with seven bedrooms, six bathrooms and space for fourteen. The first floor is a complete home of its own; the second and third floors hold the main residence and the rooftop terrace, and a private elevator connects all three. Grandparents, parents and kids get to be together without being on top of each other.

@graph.description: The best things to do in Playa Flamingo, Costa Rica: Gold Coast beaches, catamaran sails, Catalina Islands diving, day trips and seasonal events, all minutes from Casa Nina.

@graph.name: Playa Flamingo
@graph.description: A calm, white-sand crescent on the Pacific. Every distance on this page is measured from the villa’s front door.

@graph.name: Things to do around Playa Flamingo

item.name: Playa Flamingo
item.description: The home beach: a protected white-sand crescent with water calm enough for every age, and the sunsets the coast is named for.

item.name: Playa Potrero
item.description: A long, quiet stretch around the bay with gentle water and low-key beach bars. The locals’ evening walk.

item.name: Brasilito
item.description: The working beach town next door: fishing boats pulled up on the shore, a sleepy plaza, and dinner with your feet in the sand.

item.name: Playa Conchal
item.description: Sand made of crushed shells and the clearest turquoise water in the region. Bring the snorkels.

item.name: Playa Penca
item.description: A small, sheltered cove past Potrero that rarely draws a crowd. Shallow, still, and made for little ones.

item.name: Playa Grande
item.description: A wilder, protected shore inside Las Baulas National Park. Surf by day, then join a guided night walk to watch leatherback turtles nest, October to March.

item.name: The sunset catamaran
item.description: Board at Flamingo or Potrero for an afternoon down the coast, with a snorkel stop, an open bar, and the sun dropping behind the Catalinas. The one everyone remembers.

item.name: Sportfishing
item.description: Half- and full-day charters run for sailfish, marlin, roosterfish, tuna and mahi from a coast with a serious billfish reputation.

item.name: The Catalina Islands
item.description: Volcanic islets with some of the Pacific’s best diving and snorkeling. Giant mantas cruise through November to April; white-tip sharks, rays and turtles hold the fort year-round.

item.name: Learn to surf
item.description: The forgiving breaks at Tamarindo and Playa Grande built Costa Rica’s surf reputation. Lessons run daily, boards included, all levels welcome.

item.name: Kayak & paddleboard
item.description: Flamingo and Potrero bays sit glassy until midday, which makes for easy paddling across all ages. Gear is delivered straight to the beach.

item.name: Canopy zip-lining
item.description: Coastal canopy runs crowned by a dual zipline over the ocean, one of the longest in the country, with a sloth sanctuary and botanical garden waiting below.

item.name: Horseback riding
item.description: Guided rides along the sand at low tide or up into the dry-forest hills, paced for confident riders and first-timers alike.

item.name: ATV & UTV tours
item.description: Quads and side-by-sides on ridge tracks and back roads, with lookouts over the whole bay along the way.

item.name: Championship golf
item.description: A Robert Trent Jones II course threaded through the dry forest above Conchal beach. Clubs and tee times arranged.

item.name: Spa, at the villa
item.description: Massages, facials and full spa days set up poolside or on the beach. The therapists come to you.

item.name: Rincón de la Vieja
item.description: An active volcano ringed by fumaroles, waterfalls and hanging bridges. Pair the national park with thermal hot springs and mineral mud baths at Vandara for the complete day.

item.name: Palo Verde river safari
item.description: A slow boat on the Tempisque through one of Central America’s great wetlands, with monkeys and crocodiles on the banks and more than 280 bird species overhead.

item.name: Llanos de Cortés
item.description: A wide curtain waterfall with a sandy pool you can swim in. It is the easiest add-on to any inland day, and a favourite with kids.

item.name: Arenal & Monteverde
item.description: The volcano and the cloud forest sit about three hours inland. The concierge arranges the hotels, transport and guides for a two- or three-day loop, and the villa will be ready when you return.

mainEntity.name: How do we get from the airport?

acceptedAnswer.text: Liberia International (LIR) is about an hour away, and every Casa Nina booking includes airport pick-up and drop-off.

mainEntity.name: Do we need to rent a car?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Golf carts (4 or 6 passenger) are street-legal on all local roads, and the concierge arranges cart or car rentals in all different sizes.
December to April for guaranteed sun and the full social season. May to November for green hills, full waterfalls, quieter beaches and better value.
Our concierge team, included with every stay. Charters, chefs, drivers and guides are arranged before you land.
